How we know

Fair Wheel Bikes’ group rides page still gives the Shootout’s start table (6:30 am from the first Saturday of September, 7:00 am from the second Saturday of October, 7:30 am from the second Saturday of November, 7:00 am from the first Saturday of March, 6:30 am from the first Saturday of April, 6:00 am from the third Saturday of April) and the start near University Boulevard & Euclid Avenue; the listed point was about 2 miles north of that corner, so it is moved to the intersection (OpenStreetMap geometry for E University Blvd and N Euclid Ave, fetched Oct 4, 2026).

First time on this ride? Here’s the drill
Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 7:00 am. Tell whoever’s leading that you’re new.
Pace
The easiest pace the host lists is 16–20 mph: brisk — you’ll want some fitness. It’s a drop ride: if you can’t hold the pace, you’ll finish alone. Fine if you know your speed. Not a first ride.
Check
Look at the host’s website the day of — that’s where cancellations, weather calls and start changes get posted.

About the The Shootout group ride

The Shootout is a road group ride in Tucson, AZ. It rolls every Saturday at 7:00 am from University Blvd & Euclid Ave.

Tucson’s famous fast Saturday road ride. Three groups leave a few minutes apart on the same route south of town. It is self-supported and riders separate by pace. Not a beginner ride. The 16–20 mph group is the friendliest option.
